Initial reaction rates v (uM/min) of a purified enzyme were measured at substrate concentrations S (uM) (no inhibitor, I = 0). Each condition was measured in duplicate; rates carry additive measurement noise.

The data table has 16 rows with columns: S, v. Your model will be used to predict rates at substrate levels outside the measured range.

Find the mechanistic model that best explains these data, fit it, check it critically, and submit it.

I'm estimating Vmax at about 10 and a half-max near 5, which puts Km around 3, but checking S=2 gives a velocity that's too low. So I'm trying a smaller Km of 1.5 and testing it at S=0.25.

I'm checking the rest of the fit: Vmax 10, Km 1.5 tracks the data well at each substrate level, with the top end around 9.2 to 9.6. Vmax 9.8 with Km 1.5 looks good enough, and there's no sign of sigmoidal behavior or substrate inhibition, so I'll go with Michaelis-Menten using those values.
